title: Design: multi-region collaborative editing with data residency

defects.description: Addresses region-based data partitioning as a hard requirement (not a single global database) to satisfy EU data residency.
Addresses conflict resolution for concurrent edits specifically (e.g. CRDTs, operational transformation), not just "use a database with locking".

Addresses the tension between strong consistency and the sub-200ms latency requirement explicitly (e.g. strong within-region, eventual/async across regions), rather than assuming one global consistency model.
Addresses durable, replicated audit-log writes (e.g. append-only log acknowledged before commit) so an edit event cannot be lost even across a regional outage.
Explicitly addresses what happens during a regional network partition/outage rather than assuming the network is always available.
Addresses cross-region shared metadata (e.g. user directory, permissions) in a way that does not violate the EU-data-residency constraint.
